articles.title: Webb's controversial 'little red dots' may finally have an explanation
articles.description: Astronomers may have solved one of the biggest mysteries uncovered by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), using sophisticated simulations to show that enigmatic objects known as "little red dots" (LRDs) are likely the birthplaces of the first supermassive black holes.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers may have solved the mystery of JWST's 'little red dots,' potentially explaining unexpected early galaxy discoveries. This breakthrough resolves one of the telescope's most intriguing findings.

articles.title: Gravitational waves hint at black holes born from failed supernovae
articles.description: When the most massive stars in the universe die, they often detonate in fiery supernovae, dramatically blasting most of their matter into space. The remaining stellar cores collapse into neutron stars and, sometimes, black holes. However, theories suggest that some massive stars might die without a bang, instead directly collapsing inward to become neutron stars or black holes.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Gravitational wave observations suggest black holes can form from failed supernovae, offering new insights into stellar death and black hole formation. This discovery expands our understanding of extreme cosmic objects.

articles.title: NASA reveals bold new plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028
articles.description: NASA has revealed an accelerated plan to land astronauts on the Moon in 2028, with SpaceX and Blue Origin developing competing lunar landers and a crucial orbital test scheduled for 2027. Faster rocket preparations, new lightweight spacesuits, and redesigned missions could help pave the way for a permanent lunar presence and future human exploration of Mars.
articles.summary: NASA announces an accelerated plan to return astronauts to the Moon in 2028 with SpaceX and Blue Origin support, marking a landmark achievement in human space exploration. This ambitious timeline represents a major milestone in lunar return missions.

articles.title: Caltech robot makes history by building a structure in space
articles.description: For the first time, a robot has autonomously built part of a structure in space, demonstrating a breakthrough that could fundamentally change space exploration. The technology could one day allow scientists to construct enormous telescopes, communications antennas, and solar power stations in orbit, far beyond the size limits of today's rockets.
articles.summary: A Caltech robot autonomously builds a structure in space for the first time, demonstrating breakthrough technology for future space construction and habitation. This historic achievement opens new possibilities for off-world infrastructure development.

articles.title: SpaceX moves Starship Flight 15 booster to launch pad for 'squeeze test' ahead of epic double-catch attempt (photos)
articles.description: SpaceX has moved its Starship Super Heavy booster to the pad to prep for the next test flight of the megarocket, a historic mission scheduled to launch this Friday (Nov. 13).
articles.summary: SpaceX has positioned its Super Heavy booster for Flight 15, preparing for a historic double-catch landing test that represents a major milestone in reusable rocket technology. This achievement demonstrates unprecedented progress in making space transportation more efficient and sustainable.

articles.title: SpaceX Starship Flight 15 live updates: Super Heavy rocket moved to launch pad for 1st Starship double landing test
articles.description: Follow live updates as SpaceX attempts its Starship Flight 15 test flight with first double landings.
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 is underway with the Super Heavy booster attempting its first-ever double landing test, a revolutionary achievement in rocket reusability. This milestone represents a transformative moment in spaceflight capability and efficiency.

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 to Cross Historic One Light-Day Milestone on Nov. 18
articles.description: Traveling one light-day took the space probe 49 years. it would take a human 612,015 years to walk that distance.
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 is set to cross the historic one light-day milestone on November 18, marking nearly 50 years of extraordinary interstellar travel. This achievement demonstrates humanity's remarkable capability to explore the cosmos.

articles.title: NASA unveils $10B Moon base contract as SpaceX, Blue Origin join lunar gold rush
articles.description: NASA announced Saturday that Elon Musk’s SpaceX, Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin and six other aerospace companies are eligible to compete for up to $10 billion in lunar delivery contracts as the agency advances plans to establish a permanent base on the moon. The an…
articles.summary: NASA announces a $10 billion Moon base contract with SpaceX, Blue Origin, and six other aerospace companies, accelerating humanity's return to the lunar surface. This landmark collaboration represents a new era of lunar exploration and commercial space partnership.

articles.title: NASA Invites Media, Public to Join Voyager 1 One-Light Day Activities
articles.description: Launched nearly 50 years ago in 1977, NASA’s Voyager 1 on Wednesday, Nov. 18 will have traveled one light-day from Earth, which is more than 16 billion miles (25.9 billion kilometers). Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, and any light from Earth would take 24 hours to reach the spacecraft. NASA will highlight […]
articles.summary: NASA celebrates Voyager 1's historic milestone of traveling one light-day from Earth nearly 50 years after its 1977 launch, inviting the public to join commemorative activities.

articles.title: NASA Scientists Show How Gravitational Waves Can Reveal New Worlds
articles.description: The LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna) observatory, now in development, will detect gravitational waves, the tiny ripples in space-time caused by orbiting masses. Now two studies led by NASA astrophysicists show in new detail how LISA could reveal a new and unique population of exoplanets — worlds beyond our solar system — throughout our galaxy.  […]
articles.summary: NASA scientists demonstrate how the upcoming LISA observatory will use gravitational wave detection to reveal previously unknown worlds and advance our understanding of the universe.

articles.title: Automated Assembly in Space is the Future and NOM4D is Showing the Way
articles.description: The ability to build large structures in space is maturing. The ISS, Mir, and Tiangong were built in space from pre-constructed modules, but a new program called NOM4D is taking space construction to the next level. It recently showed that a simple robot can create truss-like structures in space from premade components. Is the sky the limit for NOM4D?
articles.summary: NOM4D technology demonstrates that automated assembly in space is maturing as a viable capability, building upon decades of on-orbit construction experience from the ISS, Mir, and Tiangong.

articles.title: First Direct Measurement of Cosmic Hydrogen Could Change How We Map the Universe
articles.description: The MeerKLASS international collaboration achieves the first direct measurement of the large-scale clustering of cosmic hydrogen in the Universe.
articles.summary: The MeerKLASS collaboration achieves the first direct measurement of cosmic hydrogen clustering at large scales, potentially revolutionizing how astronomers map the universe.

articles.title: A Perseverance Experiment Could Help Astronauts Prepare for Dust Storms on Mars
articles.description: Researchers at Washington University examined how dust interacts with the spacesuit swatches on the Perseverance Rover. Future missions to Mars require that planners account for the effects of dust exposure on humans and materials.
articles.summary: Perseverance Rover researchers study how Martian dust interacts with spacesuits to prepare astronauts for future dust storms on Mars. This practical research directly supports human exploration readiness.

articles.title: How the cosmic environment depletes galaxies of their gas
articles.description: An international team of researchers, led by Jonathan Freundlich (University of Strasbourg, Astronomical Observatory), has revealed how a dense cosmic environment depletes galaxies of their gas. By mapping the molecular gas in a galaxy group located 7 billion light-years away, they found that the galaxies in this group harbor, on average, gas reservoirs reduced by more than half compared to similar isolated galaxies. The results of this study are published in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: An international research team led by Jonathan Freundlich discovers how cosmic environments deplete galaxies of gas, revealing fundamental insights into galaxy evolution. This advances our understanding of large-scale cosmic processes.

articles.title: Earth's 'core carbon' may have come from the far reaches of the solar system
articles.description: A new study suggests that most of Earth's carbon originated in the outer solar system and didn't arrive here until the late stages of planetary development. The study, led by researchers at Yale and Columbia, is based upon an analysis of magma droplets called "melt inclusions" from historic volcano eruptions in Hawaii, including the Keanakākoʻi eruptions from 1500 to 1840 and the Kīlauea Iki eruption in 1959.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A new study reveals that Earth's carbon likely originated in the outer solar system and arrived during the planet's formation. This discovery reshapes our understanding of our planet's composition and origins.

articles.title: Simulated moon dust turned into LEGO-like blocks for settlements
articles.description: Permanent structures on the moon could start with something already there: lunar dust. New research from the University of Arkansas shows that pure regolith, the loose material that covers the moon, could be 3D-printed into LEGO-like bricks. Using it for construction could reduce what NASA needs to send from Earth as it works toward future lunar settlements.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Researchers transform simulated lunar dust into LEGO-like building blocks for future moon settlements, demonstrating innovative construction methods using in-situ resources. This breakthrough brings permanent lunar habitation closer to reality.

articles.title: Mysterious gas leaks suggest Mars may still be volcanically alive
articles.description: Mysterious gas emissions and fresh volcanic fissures suggest that Mars may not be geologically dead after all, with hot magma potentially still active deep underground. The discovery could point to hidden pockets of warmth and chemical energy capable of supporting microbial life beneath the Red Planet’s surface.
articles.summary: Fresh evidence including mysterious gas emissions and volcanic fissures suggests Mars may still be geologically and volcanically active. This exciting discovery reveals Mars as a more dynamic world than previously thought.

articles.title: NASA’s Swift telescope falls to Earth after nearly 22 years in space
articles.description: After nearly 22 years of exploring the universe’s most violent explosions, NASA’s Swift Observatory has re-entered Earth’s atmosphere over Indonesia. Originally designed to last just two years, the pioneering space telescope transformed our understanding of black holes, exploding stars, and mysterious cosmic outbursts.
articles.summary: After 22 years of groundbreaking observations of the universe's most violent explosions, NASA's Swift Observatory completes its mission and re-enters Earth's atmosphere. This legacy mission marks the end of an extraordinary chapter in high-energy astronomy.

articles.title: Einstein's equations reveal how gravity could break, reconnect, and release energy
articles.description: More than a century after Einstein revolutionized our understanding of gravity, scientists have uncovered a surprising new phenomenon hidden within his equations. Researchers at Columbia University and Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez have identified a theoretical process called "gravitational reconnection," in which structures within gravitational fields can break apart and reconnect, transferring energy into matter.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered new insights into how gravity behaves according to Einstein's equations, revealing mechanisms for energy release through gravitational phenomena. This breakthrough expands our century-old understanding of gravity's fundamental nature.

articles.title: NASA is racing against time to save the Hubble Space Telescope
articles.description: NASA is exploring a daring plan to save the legendary Hubble Space Telescope from its eventual fiery plunge into Earth's atmosphere. After more than 35 years of groundbreaking discoveries, Hubble is slowly losing altitude, and without intervention, it could fall back to Earth as early as 2033 or 2034. To keep the iconic observatory operating, NASA is asking private space companies to propose innovative ways to boost Hubble into a higher orbit, upgrade its capabilities, or safely dispose of it when its mission finally ends.
articles.summary: NASA is developing an innovative plan to rescue the iconic Hubble Space Telescope from deorbiting, extending the life of one of astronomy's most celebrated instruments. This bold mission represents humanity's commitment to preserving key scientific assets in space.

articles.title: Uranus has a weird magnetic field that's stumped scientists for 40 years — we may finally know why
articles.description: The lopsided magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune could be the product of extreme conditions inside the planets, increasing the electrical conductivity that enhances the dynamo effect.
articles.summary: Scientists may have finally solved a 40-year mystery about Uranus's unusual magnetic field, revealing it could be caused by extreme internal conditions. This breakthrough deepens our understanding of ice giant planetary dynamics.

articles.title: NASA opens applications for astronauts who will live on the Moon
articles.description: If you ever wanted to earn a solid wage by living and working on another world, now's your chance. NASA has put out a call for a new generation of ast...
articles.summary: NASA has opened applications for astronauts to live and work on the Moon, inviting the next generation of space explorers to participate in lunar missions. This represents an exciting opportunity for humanity's expansion beyond Earth.

articles.title: Physicists step closer to the 'Zeptoverse' after 42-year particle search
articles.description: Physicists have found evidence of a particle decay so rare that it is expected to occur only around once in every 10 billion "beauty" particles. The result, from the upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN's Large Hadron Collider (LHC), follows a search spanning mor…
articles.summary: Physicists have detected evidence of an extraordinarily rare particle decay after a 42-year search, occurring approximately once in every 10 billion interactions. This landmark discovery validates theoretical predictions and advances particle physics understanding.

articles.title: Step inside the zeptoverse: British scientists use the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside a minuscule world where exotic particles may be hiding
articles.description: British scientists have used the Large Hadron Collider to peer inside the minuscule world of the zeptoverse.
articles.summary: British scientists at the Large Hadron Collider have explored the zeptoverse to search for exotic particles in the minuscule subatomic world. This groundbreaking research expands our understanding of fundamental physics at the smallest scales.

articles.title: The Vera Rubin Has Found Two More of the Milky Way's Dim Satellites
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory has detected two more of the Milky Ways' dim, hard to see satellites. One is an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy, and one is a globular cluster. Each one is a missing piece of the puzzle in the Milky Way's merger history. By finding more of…
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory has discovered two additional dim satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way. These findings help astronomers better map our galactic neighborhood and understand galaxy formation.

articles.title: NASA is hiring astronauts for future Moon missions: Who can apply, what tests must you pass and how to get selected?
articles.description: NASA is recruiting its next class of astronauts, with selected candidates potentially preparing for future Moon missions and living at a lunar base. The agency is accepting applications from qualified US citizens, including candidates with master's-level nurs…
articles.summary: NASA is recruiting a new class of astronauts for future Moon missions, opening opportunities for qualified candidates to participate in humanity's next great adventure. Selected astronauts will help write the next chapter of space exploration.

articles.title: NASA is hiring! Aspiring astronauts offered a surprising $164,000 salary to work on the Moon: ‘Write the next chapter of human spaceflight’
articles.description: NASA last opened applications in 2024, selecting 10 astronaut candidates from more than 8,000 applications.
articles.summary: NASA is hiring astronauts with a competitive salary of $164,000 to support lunar missions and advance human spaceflight. The selection process is highly competitive, drawing thousands of passionate space explorers.

articles.title: Depuis des années, cet astéroïde accélère de façon inexpliquée : quelque chose modifie sa trajectoire et personne ne sait encore quoi
articles.description: Un petit astéroïde défie les modèles : 1998 KY26 accélère d’une manière que la gravité seule peine à expliquer. L’hypothèse de la comète sombre a été avancée. Mais une nouvelle étude vient brouiller les pistes.
articles.summary: The asteroid 1998 KY26 is accelerating in ways that gravity alone cannot explain, presenting an intriguing cosmic mystery. Scientists continue investigating this enigmatic object to understand the forces shaping our solar system.

articles.title: Diese Helikopterdrohne fliegt zum Saturnmond Titan – und dein Name könnte mit an Bord sein
articles.description:
Die Nasa wirbt mit einer kuriosen Aktion für ihre Mission zum Saturnmond Titan: Ihr könnt euren Namen auf einer Drohne hinterlassen. Das steckt dahinter.
weiterlesen auf t3n.de
articles.summary: NASA is inviting people to have their names travel aboard a helicopter drone destined for Saturn's moon Titan. This exciting mission will explore one of the solar system's most fascinating and mysterious worlds.

articles.title: NASA to Welcome Expedition 74 Astronauts Home at Space Center Houston
articles.description: NASA will welcome home the Expedition 74 crew during a public event at Space Center Houston following their return from a long-duration mission aboard the International Space Station. NASA astronauts Jessica Meir, Jack Hathaway, and Chris Williams; ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot; and Roscosmos cosmonauts Sergey Kud‑Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev will share mission […]
articles.summary: NASA hosts a public welcome-home event at Space Center Houston for the Expedition 74 astronauts returning from their mission aboard the International Space Station.
